content.title: About
content.content: Zucchini (Cucurbita pepo), also called courgette, is a summer squash with a tender, thin green skin and mild, slightly sweet flesh, harvested while still immature. It originated in the Americas and is now eaten worldwide. Zucchini is eaten raw or cooked and used in sautés, soups, baked goods, and as a low-carbohydrate substitute for pasta.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Zucchini is botanically a fruit, though it is used as a vegetable in cooking.
Zucchini is harvested while young and tender, unlike winter squashes.
Zucchini flowers are edible and are often stuffed and fried.
Zucchini can be spiralized into noodles often called zoodles.
Zucchini plants produce a large number of fruits quickly during the growing season.

items.title: Provides vitamin C and vitamin B6
items.content: These vitamins support the immune system and metabolism.

items.title: Contains potassium and manganese
items.content: These minerals support normal blood pressure and metabolism.

items.title: Contains lutein and zeaxanthin
items.content: These plant pigments, especially in the skin, are associated with eye health.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Zucchini contributes fiber that supports digestion.

items.title: Hydrating and low in calories
items.content: Zucchini is mostly water and low in calories.

items.title: Bitter zucchini
items.content: Rarely, zucchini can contain high levels of bitter cucurbitacins that can cause stomach upset. Discard zucchini that tastes very bitter.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large amounts may cause gas or bloating in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Zucchini allergy is uncommon but can occur.

items.title: Overcooking
items.content: Overcooked zucchini becomes mushy and watery, and frying makes it absorb a lot of oil.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Zucchini can be sliced raw into salads, grilled, roasted, sautéed, steamed, spiralized into noodles, or grated into fritters, muffins, and breads. It can be stuffed or added to soups, stews, and pasta sauces. The skin and seeds are edible, so no peeling is needed.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unwashed zucchini in the refrigerator crisper drawer in a perforated bag, where it keeps for about a week. Wash it just before use. Grated zucchini can be blanched or squeezed dry and frozen for baking and soups.
